chunks: And Ṣafwān narrated from Murāzim, from some of our companions:
Regarding a man who gives something from his wealth during his illness
He said: “If he makes it distinct and hands it over, then it is valid; but if he bequeaths it, then it is from the one-third.”

key_terms.أَبَانَ بِهِ: he clearly separated and effected it as an actual transfer
key_terms.أَوْصَى بِهِ: he made it a bequest to be carried out after death
key_terms.الثُّلُثِ: one-third of the estate, the limit for a bequest without further approval
key_terms.فِي مَرَضِهِ: during his illness, especially in the context of legal rulings on end-of-life wealth disposition

ai.seo_question: Is a gift made during illness treated differently from a bequest in Islamic inheritance law?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about disposing of wealth during a final illness. A transfer that is clearly executed and separated is valid, while a mere bequest takes effect only within the limit of one-third of the estate.
